purpose: Present two labelled answers to one question and ask for a single declared verdict, so position, verbosity, style, repetition, transitivity and self-preference can each be measured by counting verdicts.
system: You are comparing two answers to the same question. Judge only which answer is better; do not rewrite either. Answer with JSON and nothing else.

question.description: The question both answers respond to.

answers.description: The labelled answer block, built by the harness so that a swapped presentation differs from its original in order alone.

attribution.description: An optional line naming whose answer is whose. Empty for a blinded presentation; the self-preference test is the only case that fills it, and the difference between the two is the measurement.

expectations: A single JSON object carrying 'choice' as 'A', 'B' or 'tie'.

metadata.author: suite
metadata.change_reason: First version: native.judge needs one presentation prompt whose only variable across a swap is the order of the answer block, so that a difference in verdict is a difference in position and nothing else.
